analysis_plan.query_summary: Emergency disaster assessment for Tropical Cyclone Arnab to evaluate severity, affected area in km², and immediate risk.
analysis_plan.priority_notes: High priority emergency disaster assessment requiring rapid response.

recommended_datasets.name: Sentinel-1
recommended_datasets.why_recommended: C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery penetrates clouds and adverse weather conditions during tropical cyclones, making it the primary dataset for flood extent and severity mapping.

recommended_datasets.name: Sentinel-2
recommended_datasets.why_recommended: High-resolution optical multispectral imagery provides complementary NDWI and vegetation index analysis once cloud cover clears following the cyclone.

recommended_datasets.name: GADM Administrative Boundaries
recommended_datasets.why_recommended: Provides exact district and sub-district polygons (Level-2) for precise spatial clipping and affected area calculation in km².

gis_processing.gis_summary: Executed emergency GIS processing for Tropical Cyclone Arnab. Administrative boundary polygons (GADM Level-2) were successfully buffered by 5.0 km to define immediate risk zones, and precise area calculations were performed yielding a total assessed area of 3,178,196.81 km² across 676 features. Sentinel-1 SAR flood analysis and Sentinel-2 NDWI spectral indices from Google Earth Engine were integrated for inundation assessment. An interactive web-ready HTML disaster assessment map was generated for visualization.

earth_observation.change_summary: Extensive inundation and surface water expansion across Andhra Pradesh, India, following Tropical Cyclone Arnab. Water body extent surged from a baseline of 21,046.33 km² to 53,579.92 km² during the event window (November 2024), yielding an incremental inundation area of 32,533.59 km².
detected_anomalies: Catastrophic surface water expansion (32,533.59 km² incremental inundation)
Severe positive shift in regional NDWI mean values from -0.2828 (baseline) to -0.1638 (flood period)
Widespread agricultural and low-lying land submergence
earth_observation.event_summary: Tropical Cyclone Arnab triggered torrential rainfall and severe coastal storm surges, resulting in catastrophic flooding across low-lying districts of Andhra Pradesh, submerging over 32,500 square kilometers of additional land beyond normal baseline water bodies.
earth_observation.gee_interpretation: Sentinel-2 optical multispectral analysis (NDWI threshold > 0.2) captured a massive surge in surface water accumulation. The comparison between pre-cyclone baseline (Sept-Oct 2024) and event period (Nov 2024) demonstrates widespread flooding classified as CATASTROPHIC severity.
